mpa.about:
Privacy

The page runs locally in your browser. Nothing you enter is sent to a server or processed online. The app keeps one autosaved copy of the current session in this browser’s local storage, only so it can offer to restore it after an accidental close; it is dropped after 24 hours, and “Clear session” at the top of the page (or “Discard” in the restore bar) removes it at once. Exported session files stay wherever you save them.

Research use only

For research purposes only, not for routine clinical use. NephroTDM is not a certified medical device, and none of its models has been clinically validated by this project. Validate against prospective data before routine use. Interpretation needs clinical judgement and local protocols.

The app never recommends, selects or optimizes a dose. It estimates exposure with its uncertainty and lets you explore what a candidate maintenance dose would do. That decision stays yours.

What this app estimates for mycophenolic acid

Steady-state mycophenolic acid AUC0–12h, the AUC over a 12-hour dosing interval at steady state (regimens with another interval are reported as their 12-hour equivalent, AUC₁₂ = AUC0–ₓ × 12/ₓ). It comes from a population PK model and limited sampling and is reported as a median with a 5–95% interval. Alongside it: the probability that AUC lies inside the therapeutic window, P(AUC > lower bound), P(AUC < upper bound), and a predicted trough C(τ). Trough is informational only: there is no trough target.

Therapeutic window (AUC0–12h)

The default window is prefilled from the source below and can be overridden per patient. The window is the only pair of numbers that turns a PK estimate into a clinical judgement, so its provenance is stated explicitly.

  • Kidney transplant, MMF + CNI (adult and pediatric): 30–60 mg·h/L. Bergan S et al. Personalized therapy for mycophenolate: consensus report by the International Association of Therapeutic Drug Monitoring and Clinical Toxicology. Ther Drug Monit 2021;43(2):150–197 (grade B, II).
  • Heart transplantation: AUC0–12h > 36 mg·h/L is cited; edit the window if that is your practice.
  • Lupus nephritis (proliferative): aim near 50 mg·h/L (prefer 45–60, not the transplant lower bound of 30). Wuttiputhanun T et al. Lupus Sci Med 2024;11:e001093.
  • Lung, HSCT, EC-MPS, beyond the first posttransplant year: evidence-based windows differ or are lacking, do not leave the kidney-transplant default in place without considering this.

Both bounds are used: therapeutic probability is P(lower < AUC < upper). The window is a clinical input you control, not a hidden model assumption.

Limited sampling

The IATDMCT consensus recommends MAP-Bayesian estimation from a limited sampling strategy rather than a trough alone, and rather than a regression equation. Typical schemes:

  • MMF: at least two concentrations; typical three-point LSS at ~20 min, 1 h and 3 h post-dose.
  • EC-MPS: three to four samples; typical ~1.5 h, 2 h, 4 h (± 6 h).
  • Trough-only is discouraged: C0 correlates poorly with AUC because of enterohepatic recirculation, and the consensus recommends against C0-guided dose adjustment.
  • Below the limit of quantification: a result reported as “< LLOQ” cannot be used, omit that sample. Do not enter zero or the LLOQ as a concentration; either biases the AUC (a zero by about −27%).

Immunoassays (EMIT, PETINIA, CEDIA) overestimate MPA versus LC-MS/MS; a model should be used with the analytical technique it was developed on, and this app cannot correct for the assay.

Weighting of older samples (optional, off by default)

Under advanced fitting options, older measurements can be given a larger residual error so that they influence the individual fit less than recent ones. A concentration describes the patient as they were on the day it was drawn; the further back that is, the less well it describes them now.

Each sample’s residual standard deviation is multiplied by a factor that grows with age from the newest sample and saturates at a preset M: low ×1.5, medium ×2, high ×3. The newest sample is never inflated, and an old sample is down-weighted but never discarded. Neither M nor the time constant is estimated from the patient’s data, they are a clinical judgement about how much to trust older measurements, made explicit and printed in the report.

Two cautions. Widening the residual error widens the reported intervals, so a forecast made with this option on is less certain, not more. And age is not the same thing as relevance: to set aside a sample you believe is unrepresentative, exclude it explicitly rather than relying on its date.

Models

For each model, assumptions and simplifications relative to its source are listed. Read them before clinical interpretation. Time is in hours everywhere in this app (engine, plots, fields, session and report).

Mycophenolic acid

de Winter BCM, van Gelder T, Glander P, et al. Population Pharmacokinetics of Mycophenolic Acid: A Comparison between Enteric-Coated Mycophenolate Sodium and Mycophenolate Mofetil in Renal Transplant Recipients. Clin Pharmacokinet 2008;47(12):827–838.

Two-compartment model with first-order absorption and lag time, fitted to 3764 concentrations from 259 maintenance renal-transplant recipients (4–257 months post-transplant). Formulation is a covariate on absorption: EC-MPS is absorbed later and more variably than MMF (trimodal morning lag-time). No patient covariates besides formulation; dosing is absolute mg (no allometric weight scaling). Validated internally (1000 bootstraps + visual predictive check) on pooled data.

Tacrolimus

Disposition is modelled on plasma concentrations and scaled to fat-free mass; whole-blood concentrations follow from the haematocrit. CYP3A5 genotype and prednisolone dose are covariates. Reported: steady-state AUC0–12h and trough, as measured (actual) and corrected to haematocrit 0.35.

Disposition parameters refer to plasma concentrations at a fat-free mass of 60 kg in a CYP3A5 non-expresser; they are scaled by fat-free mass (clearances ^0.75, volumes ^1) and whole-blood concentrations follow from the haematocrit.

  • Adult kidney-transplant recipients, immediate-release tacrolimus twice daily (Prograf). Prolonged-release products, children and other organs are not covered. The model was built on Norwegian and Australian cohorts, 23–71 years, haematocrit about 0.25–0.43, prednisolone 5–36 mg/day
  • Intended for use some days after transplantation. The model’s first-day bioavailability effect (×2.68) is left out, so a result computed in the first week or two is biased upward. For a typical patient the real trough is about 20–50 % higher than the model expects on day 4, about 5–15 % on day 7, and 1 % or less after two weeks
  • Reported values are steady state on a typical day (occasion effects at zero), at the haematocrit of the most recent sample. A single day varies around them by about 23 % (between-occasion variability of bioavailability). One sampling day cannot fix the steady-state AUC more tightly than about ×/÷ 1.4 (5–95 %); two days give ×/÷ 1.3
  • Corrected to haematocrit 0.35 means the whole-blood concentration this patient would show with the same plasma concentration at a haematocrit of 0.35, computed with the model’s red-cell binding equation
  • CYP3A5 genotype unknown is treated as a non-expresser (no mixture). Expression changes clearance by +30 % and bioavailability by −18 %
  • Variability from the paper’s Table 2 (CVs, read as ω = CV; correlations CL–V1 0.43 and CL–Q 0.62). The V1–Q correlation is not published and is taken as the product of the other two (0.27)
  • Occasion = calendar day. Each sampled day (up to the 12 most recent) gets its own effect on bioavailability and on the absorption rate; days without a sample are taken at zero
  • Assay: LC-MS/MS, or Abbott CMIA via the model authors’ conversion (one laboratory, 43 pairs); other immunoassays cannot be used. The immunoassay line is valid for 3.6–14.4 µg/L
  • Not in the model: renal and liver function, age (bioavailability rises 1.4 %/year above 45 in the data but the effect was left out as empirical), CYP3A inhibitors and inducers, food, adherence. The AUC was never evaluated externally in the source study (its external evaluation used troughs in the first three weeks)
  • Estimated with NONMEM FOCE-I

Windows: The windows start at the standard for adult kidney recipients. Change or clear them to suit your patient or protocol; the Tacrolimus background dialog lists the consensus sets. µg/L is the same as ng/mL, and µg·h/L the same as ng·h/mL.

mpa.background:
Mycophenolic acid (MPA) exposure varies several-fold between patients on the same dose. Under-exposure is associated with acute rejection; over-exposure with toxicity. The IATDMCT consensus therefore recommends measuring AUC0–12h, not trough, to personalize mycophenolate in the first posttransplant year. Routine AUC-guided dosing for every kidney recipient is not mandated (consider it especially in high-risk patients), but when TDM is used, AUC is the metric.

Reference values

Default in this app: 30–60 mg·h/L (kidney transplant, MMF + CNI, grade B, II). Edit the window if your indication differs, lupus nephritis and nephrotic syndrome both need a higher floor than the transplant lower bound of 30.

SettingTargetNote
Kidney transplant (adult & pediatric), MMF + CNIAUC0–12h 30–60 mg·h/LB, II, this app’s default
Liver transplantAUC0–12h 30–60 mg·h/Lsupported by RCT
Heart transplantAUC0–12h > 36 mg·h/LC, III, one-sided
Lung transplantnone establisheddo not reuse 30–60 silently
Adult HSCTAUC0–24h > 30 mg·h/Ldifferent interval
Lupus nephritis (proliferative)AUC0–12h around 50 mg·h/L (prefer 45–60, not 30)responders 51 vs non-responders 30; 40–60 ≈ 70–80% remission
Nephrotic syndrome (pediatric FRNS/SDNS)AUC0–12h > 45–50 mg·h/Lhigher than the pediatric transplant range of 30–60; needed to prevent relapses

In lupus nephritis, a 2024 meta-analysis found renal responders at mean AUC 51 mg·h/L versus 30 in non-responders. Most included studies targeted above 30 or 45; meta-regression linked 40–60 mg·h/L with a 70–80% remission rate. Do not leave the kidney-transplant lower bound of 30 in place for LN, prefer a window centred near 50 (e.g. 45–60). There are no RCTs of concentration-controlled versus fixed-dose MPA in LN yet.

In childhood frequently relapsing or steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome, MMF dose correlates poorly with MPA exposure. Relapses were more common when estimated AUC was < 50 mg·h/L; a higher target than in pediatric kidney transplantation (AUC0–12h > 45–50 mg·h/L) is essential to preserve remission. Guide therapy with TDM rather than a fixed mg/m² dose.

Transplant targets apply mainly to the first posttransplant year and are not validated for EC-MPS. Immunoassays overestimate MPA versus LC-MS/MS; use a model with the assay it was built on.

Why model-based (MAP-Bayesian) TDM

The consensus prefers MAP-Bayesian estimation over a regression equation because it:

  • accepts samples at the times they were actually drawn, not a fixed schedule;
  • is not locked to a 12-hour dosing interval;
  • lets you inspect the fitted concentration–time curve against the data;
  • returns an interval on AUC, not only a point estimate.

That is what this app does: individualize from a population model plus the samples you enter, then report AUC with uncertainty.

Limited sampling versus trough

There is no evidence for adjusting MMF or EC-MPS from C0. Trough correlates poorly with AUC because of enterohepatic recirculation (a secondary peak). A short limited-sampling strategy with MAP-Bayesian estimation is the recommended alternative:

FormulationMinimumTypical times after dose
MMF≥ 2 samples~20 min, 1 h, 3 h
EC-MPS3–4 samples~1.5 h, 2 h, 4 h (± 6 h)

mpa.gettingStarted:
This tool estimates steady-state mycophenolic acid AUC0–12h for one specific patient (the AUC over a 12-hour dosing interval at steady state), using their covariates and any measured concentrations you enter. Nothing you type leaves this device. There is no server involved. Keep this window open and work through the four cards on the main screen in order.

  1. Patient & covariates. This model (de Winter 2008) uses exactly one covariate: the formulation (MMF or EC-MPS), which switches absorption behaviour and the dose conversion. Doses are entered as prescribed, in product mg; the app converts to MPA content internally (×0.739 MMF, ×0.936 EC-MPS). The therapeutic AUC0–12h window defaults to 30–60 mg·h/L, the kidney-transplant value (Bergan 2021; liver transplant uses the same range). Other indications need different bounds: heart transplant >36, proliferative lupus nephritis ≈50 (prefer 45–60), childhood nephrotic syndrome >45–50, so set the bounds for your indication before reading the probabilities (“MPA TDM background” lists them all with citations).
  2. Dosing schedule & measured concentrations. Choose Full schedule if you know the actual dates and doses this patient has received, or Steady state if they are already on a stable maintenance regimen and you just want to enter the dose and interval (hours). Add measured concentrations. For MMF use at least two post-dose samples (typical limited-sampling times 20 min, 1 h, 3 h); for EC-MPS three to four (1.5 h, 2 h, 4 h ± 6 h), and note the source model’s own warning that sparse sampling is expected to be unreliable for EC-MPS, so prefer more samples across the interval there. Trough-only sampling is discouraged. A measured level is what lets the app personalize the estimate instead of just showing the population average.
  3. Forecast. Press Run forecast. The result is a predicted steady-state AUC0–12h with a 5–95% interval. If the regimen’s interval is not 12 h, the AUC is reported as its 12-hour equivalent (AUC₁₂ = AUC0–ₓ × 12/ₓ), so it always targets the therapeutic window. You also get the probability that AUC sits inside that window, and a predicted trough C(τ) with no trough target. This is a prediction, not a recommendation. The app never suggests a dose or interval; that decision stays yours. Time is in hours everywhere.
  4. Dose explorer (optional). Once you have run a forecast, this card shows what a different maintenance dose would do for this same patient, using the fit you already have. You can also choose the interval (12 h or 24 h); whatever you pick, the AUC is reported as a 12-hour equivalent (AUC₁₂ = AUC₀–x × 12/x) so it stays comparable with the window, alongside the three window probabilities and the predicted trough. Skip it if you only need the estimate for the regimen already planned.

When you are done: Print report asks for your name and advice, then builds a one-page printable summary. Export session saves the case as a file you can reopen later or hand to a colleague. If you close the tab by accident, reopening the app offers to restore what you were working on.

Curious about the model behind the numbers, the therapeutic window, or the research-use disclaimer? See About, top right.

Sampling guidance and the default window come from the IATDMCT consensus (Bergan 2021).
mpa.chartNote: Individual = this patient’s measured levels · Population = model only · red points = measurements. The therapeutic window is an AUC range (mg·h/L), shown in the results grid; it is not a concentration band on this plot. Time axis in hours after the last dose.
mpa.howto:
• AUC0–12h: the model’s estimate of steady-state mycophenolic acid exposure over one 12-hour dosing interval, with a 5–95% interval.
  • Probability in window: the chance that the true AUC0–12h falls between your chosen lower and upper bound.
  • Predicted trough: the model’s estimate of the concentration just before the next dose. There is no trough target in this app; it is shown for context only.
  • Band (5–95%): 90% plausible range for the true concentration curve. It does not include assay error, so a future measured value may fall outside it.

Privacy

The page runs locally in your browser. Nothing you enter is sent to a server or processed online. The app keeps one autosaved copy of the current session in this browser’s local storage, only so it can offer to restore it after an accidental close; it is dropped after 24 hours, and “Clear session” at the top of the page (or “Discard” in the restore bar) removes it at once. Research use only

The app never recommends, selects or optimizes a dose. It estimates exposure with its uncertainty and lets you explore what a candidate maintenance dose would do. That decision stays yours.

What this app estimates for tacrolimus

For an adult kidney transplant recipient on immediate-release tacrolimus twice daily: the steady-state whole-blood AUC0–12h and trough of the current regimen on a typical day. They come from a population PK model and the samples entered, each as a median with a 5–95% interval, as measured (actual) and corrected to a haematocrit of 0.35. If you set windows, you also get the probability of lying inside, above or below each. In the source study the AUC was not evaluated externally: its external evaluation used troughs in the first three weeks after transplantation.

What it does not cover

  • Prolonged-release tacrolimus (once daily), children, and recipients of other organs.
  • The first days after transplantation. The model’s first-day bioavailability effect is left out, so on day 4 the real trough of a typical patient is about 20–50% higher than the model expects and the steady-state AUC is overestimated. On day 7 the gap is about 5–15%, and after two weeks 1% or less.
  • Renal and liver function, age, interacting drugs (CYP3A and P-glycoprotein inhibitors and inducers), food and adherence. None of these is in the model. A stable interaction is absorbed by the patient’s own clearance; one that starts or stops inside the entered history is not.
  • Results below the limit of quantification. A result reported as “< LLOQ” cannot be used, so omit it.

Reference values for tacrolimus (adult kidney recipients, twice-daily immediate-release)

From the IATDMCT second consensus report (Brunet 2019). The windows are starting points that you can change or clear; the Tacrolimus background dialog has the same sets with a “Use this window” button each. µg/L is the same as ng/mL.

Haematocrit, assay and sampling

  • Haematocrit: tacrolimus sits in red cells, so whole blood reads higher at a higher haematocrit for the same plasma concentration, and haematocrit changes after transplantation (in the source cohort from about 0.30 to about 0.37 over the first weeks). The app reports the measured value and the value corrected to 0.35. The same windows apply to both.
  • Assay: LC-MS/MS, or Abbott CMIA converted with the model authors’ equation (LC-MS/MS = 0.80 × CMIA + 0.19 µg/L, one laboratory, 43 pairs, 3.6–14.4 µg/L CMIA). Other immunoassays cannot be used.
  • Sampling: a predose trough plus one sample 1–3 h after the dose tells the model much more about the AUC than troughs alone. Enter exact times and a haematocrit with each sample, and avoid the first 45 minutes after a dose (the model has a 25-minute lag). One sampling day cannot fix the steady-state AUC better than about ×/÷ 1.4; two days give about ×/÷ 1.3.

The consensus proposes AUC as the best TDM option early after transplantation, when immunosuppression is being minimised, in special populations and in specific clinical situations. Estimating it from a population model plus the samples you enter lets you use the sample times you actually have, not a fixed schedule, handles the haematocrit, and returns an interval rather than a single number.

  • No enterohepatic recirculation compartment (tested, not retained); slight 6-h overprediction in the VPC
  • Estimated with NONMEM first-order (FO) method

AUC window: See “MPA TDM background” for reference values and best practices for TDM.

Tacrolimus

Størset E, Holford N, Hennig S, Bergmann TK, Bergan S, Bremer S, Åsberg A, Midtvedt K, Staatz CE. Improved prediction of tacrolimus concentrations early after kidney transplantation using theory-based pharmacokinetic modelling. Br J Clin Pharmacol 2014;78(3):509–523.

Two-compartment model with first-order absorption and lag time for immediate-release tacrolimus (twice daily) in adult kidney transplant recipients (242 patients, 3100 whole-blood concentrations, mostly the first three months). Disposition is modelled on plasma concentrations and scaled to fat-free mass; whole-blood concentrations follow from the haematocrit. CYP3A5 genotype and prednisolone dose are covariates. Reported: steady-state AUC0–12h and trough, as measured (actual) and corrected to haematocrit 0.35.

Disposition parameters refer to plasma concentrations at a fat-free mass of 60 kg in a CYP3A5 non-expresser; they are scaled by fat-free mass (clearances ^0.75, volumes ^1) and whole-blood concentrations follow from the haematocrit.

  • Adult kidney-transplant recipients, immediate-release tacrolimus twice daily (Prograf). Prolonged-release products, children and other organs are not covered. The model was built on Norwegian and Australian cohorts, 23–71 years, haematocrit about 0.25–0.43, prednisolone 5–36 mg/day
  • Intended for use some days after transplantation. The model’s first-day bioavailability effect (×2.68) is left out, so a result computed in the first week or two is biased upward. For a typical patient the real trough is about 20–50 % higher than the model expects on day 4, about 5–15 % on day 7, and 1 % or less after two weeks
  • Reported values are steady state on a typical day (occasion effects at zero), at the haematocrit of the most recent sample. A single day varies around them by about 23 % (between-occasion variability of bioavailability). One sampling day cannot fix the steady-state AUC more tightly than about ×/÷ 1.4 (5–95 %); two days give ×/÷ 1.3
  • Corrected to haematocrit 0.35 means the whole-blood concentration this patient would show with the same plasma concentration at a haematocrit of 0.35, computed with the model’s red-cell binding equation
  • CYP3A5 genotype unknown is treated as a non-expresser (no mixture). Expression changes clearance by +30 % and bioavailability by −18 %
  • Variability from the paper’s Table 2 (CVs, read as ω = CV; correlations CL–V1 0.43 and CL–Q 0.62). The V1–Q correlation is not published and is taken as the product of the other two (0.27)
  • Occasion = calendar day. Each sampled day (up to the 12 most recent) gets its own effect on bioavailability and on the absorption rate; days without a sample are taken at zero
  • Assay: LC-MS/MS, or Abbott CMIA via the model authors’ conversion (one laboratory, 43 pairs); other immunoassays cannot be used. The immunoassay line is valid for 3.6–14.4 µg/L
  • Not in the model: renal and liver function, age (bioavailability rises 1.4 %/year above 45 in the data but the effect was left out as empirical), CYP3A inhibitors and inducers, food, adherence. The AUC was never evaluated externally in the source study (its external evaluation used troughs in the first three weeks)
  • Estimated with NONMEM FOCE-I

Windows: The windows start at the standard for adult kidney recipients. Change or clear them to suit your patient or protocol; the Tacrolimus background dialog lists the consensus sets. µg/L is the same as ng/mL, and µg·h/L the same as ng·h/mL.

tac.background:
Tacrolimus has a narrow therapeutic index, and exposure differs a lot between patients and from day to day in the same patient. Whole-blood trough concentrations are the routine measure. The area under the curve over a dosing interval (AUC0–12h) describes exposure more completely. The IATDMCT consensus report proposes AUC as the best TDM option early after transplantation, when immunosuppression is being minimised, in special populations and in specific clinical situations, and it grades trough targets (C0) per patient group.

Therapeutic windows

The app starts with the standard window for adult kidney recipients (trough 4–12 µg/L, AUC0–12h 150–210 µg·h/L; first set below). It is a starting point: change either bound in card 1, pick another set here, or clear a window to get intervals without probabilities. The probabilities are only as meaningful as the window you set.

Adult kidney, standard immunological risk standard
Trough 4–12 µg/L  ·  AUC0–12h 150–210 µg·h/L  ·  grade: Trough A, I; AUC lower bound B, II
Tacrolimus with mycophenolate and steroids after IL-2R blocker induction; the report prefers troughs above 7. AUC 150 is the report’s minimal threshold; 210 is the app’s choice, the upper end of the AUC range the report pairs with a trough of 8–12.
Kidney, with everolimus, months 0–2
Trough 4–7 µg/L  ·  AUC0–12h none given  ·  grade: B, II
Reduced-exposure tacrolimus plus everolimus. The report gives no AUC range for this combination.
Kidney, with everolimus, after month 2
Trough 2–4 µg/L  ·  AUC0–12h none given  ·  grade: B, II
As above, later period. No AUC range in the report.

AUC ranges matched to a trough range

Pick a trough range and the period after transplantation; the button shows the AUC0–12h range (µg·h/L) that goes with it and fills both windows. These are derived by regression of AUC on trough in 2030 routine profiles from 1000 adult kidney recipients on twice-daily tacrolimus, with the AUC itself estimated by Bayesian models (Saint-Marcoux 2013). They are not ranges tested against outcomes. “All periods” is the combination the consensus quotes. A dash means the paper gives no range for that cell.

The standard set’s trough range is a graded consensus recommendation. The AUC lower bound is the consensus’s minimal threshold, a weaker recommendation based on two small studies. The AUC upper bound is the app’s own choice (see its note). The matched AUC ranges above are the consensus’s, calculated from trough ranges and not tested against outcomes.

For patients at higher immunological risk the consensus says targets may be higher but gives no numbers; enter your protocol’s values. Targets also depend on the co-medication and local practice. For orientation, the centres behind the source model aimed at troughs of 3–7 µg/L (standard risk) and 8–12 µg/L (high risk) in Oslo, and 7–8 µg/L in Brisbane during the first three months. The windows apply to the actual and to the haematocrit-corrected values alike.

Haematocrit and the corrected value

Tacrolimus is bound to red blood cells. At the same unbound (active) concentration, whole blood reads higher the higher the haematocrit, and haematocrit changes a lot after kidney transplantation (in the source cohort it rose from about 0.30 to about 0.37 over the first weeks). The app reports both the actual whole-blood value and the value corrected to a haematocrit of 0.35: the concentration this patient would show, for the same plasma concentration, at 0.35.

Example: a patient with a trough of 4.2 µg/L at a haematocrit of 0.25 reads about 5.8 µg/L corrected. The same plasma exposure at 0.40 reads about 6.6 µg/L as measured, and again 5.8 corrected. The correction uses the red-cell binding equation of the model. The simple proportional formula (value × 0.35 / haematocrit) differs from it by 2% or less between 0.20 and 0.50.

Assay

The model was built on LC-MS/MS concentrations. Abbott CMIA (Architect) values are converted with the model authors’ own equation (LC-MS/MS = 0.80 × CMIA + 0.19 µg/L, from one laboratory, 43 sample pairs, 3.6–14.4 µg/L CMIA), and all results are shown back on the scale you choose. Other immunoassays have no conversion in the source and cannot be used. Immunoassays read higher than LC-MS/MS because they cross-react with tacrolimus metabolites.

Sampling

SamplesWhat they give the model
Predose trough onlyLittle beyond the population: the estimate shrinks towards the typical patient.
Trough plus one sample 1–3 h after the doseThe absorption phase and the peak, which tells the model far more about the AUC than troughs alone.
Troughs on several daysDay-to-day variability can be separated from the patient’s own clearance.

Enter the exact times of dose and sample and a haematocrit with each sample. Avoid the first 45 minutes after a dose: the model has a 25-minute lag with no variability. A trough drawn 10.5 or 13 h after the dose is fine, because the model predicts the 12-hour value.

One sampling day has a limit. Bioavailability varies about 23% from one day to the next in the same patient. From a single day the model cannot tell how much of a deviation belongs to the patient and how much to that day, so the steady-state AUC is known no better than about ×/÷ 1.4 (5–95%), however many samples that day holds. Two days give about ×/÷ 1.3 and three about ×/÷ 1.2. The intervals in the app show this.

tac.gettingStarted:
For one adult kidney transplant recipient on immediate-release tacrolimus twice daily, this tool estimates the steady-state AUC0–12h and trough with 5–95% intervals, from the covariates and the concentrations you enter. Both are shown as measured (actual whole blood) and corrected to a haematocrit of 0.35. Nothing you type leaves this device. Work through the four cards in order.

  1. Patient & covariates. Choose tacrolimus. Enter weight, height and sex (they give the fat-free mass the model scales to), the prednisolone dose in mg/day (0 if none), the haematocrit in L/L (0.33, not 33), and the assay the concentrations come from. CYP3A5 genotype is optional: if it is unknown, the app assumes a non-expresser. The two therapeutic windows start at the standard for adult kidney recipients; change or clear them as you need (without a window the app gives intervals but no probabilities).
  2. Dosing schedule & measured concentrations. Choose Full schedule to enter the actual doses, or Steady state for a stable regimen (dose, interval, time of the latest dose). Doses are in mg of tacrolimus. Add the samples with their exact times and haematocrit. A trough plus one sample 1–3 h after the dose tells the model much more than troughs alone. The app is meant for use some days after transplantation: the model leaves out the extra absorption of the first day, so a result from the first week or two is biased upward.
  3. Forecast. Press Run forecast. You get the steady-state AUC0–12h and trough of the current regimen on a typical day (a single day varies around that by about 23%), each with a 5–95% interval, as measured and corrected. With windows set, you also get the probability that the exposure lies inside, above or below them. These are predictions, not recommendations.
  4. Dose explorer (optional). After a forecast, this card shows what a different dose, at the same 12-hour interval, would do for this patient at steady state, using the fit you already have. It does not select or recommend a dose.

When you are done: Print report builds a one-page summary and Export session saves the case as a file. If you close the tab by accident, reopening the app offers to restore your work.

Sampling guidance and the windows are explained in the background dialog. The model and its limits are in About.

tac.howto:
• Steady-state AUC₀–12h and trough: the model’s estimate for the current regimen on a typical day, with a 5–95% interval. One sampling day cannot fix the steady-state AUC more tightly than about ×/÷ 1.4; two days give about ×/÷ 1.3.
  • Corrected to haematocrit 0.35: the whole-blood value this patient would show, for the same plasma concentration, at a haematocrit of 0.35. It removes the effect of anaemia or a high haematocrit on the reading.
  • Probability in window: shown only if you set a window; the chance that the exposure lies between your lower and upper bound.
  • Band (5–95%): 90% plausible range for the true concentration curve. It does not include assay error, so a future measured value may fall outside it.
